problem: Existing VLN agents treat each of the (typically three) instructions for a trajectory in isolation under an iid assumption, so ambiguous or under-specified instructions cause failures and generalization to unseen environments is poor.
motivation: Each annotator mentions and omits different landmarks, so a single instruction only loosely specifies the path. Treating instructions as different views of the same trajectory (multi-view learning) lets the agent eliminate hypotheses that conflict across views and reduces entropy of trajectory prediction.
key_idea: Train the navigator on multiple instructions for the same trajectory jointly (LEO): a shared language encoder gives per-instruction contexts that are merged by parameter-free pooling before action selection.
insight: Conditioning on more instructions provably lowers conditional entropy H(tau|X) <= H(tau|x_i). Even when a single instruction is used at test time, multi-instruction training generalizes better (unseen SPL 25->31), and shared encoder + mean-pooling is best in unseen environments (mean 41 SPL vs max 34, concat 28; shared 41 vs multi-arm 28), suggesting fewer parameters and conservative aggregation reduce overfitting.
method: Multi-view formulation: each of the M instructions is a view of the same trajectory label; drops the iid assumption and maximizes log pi(tau|X) jointly, with an entropy-reduction argument (appendix proof).
Shared language encoder: a single-layer LSTM (hidden 512) encodes every instruction with shared parameters, so any number of instructions can be fed at test time.

Memory-attended language context: the decoder LSTM memory h_t attends over word features of each instruction to get per-instruction textual context c_{t,i}; visual panoramic features are attended with h_{t-1}.
Aggregation: parameter-free pooling z_t = g(c_{t,1..M}) (mean, max, or concat); mean is the default.
Action selection: bilinear softmax over navigable directions using [h_t, z_t] and action embeddings (visual feature + heading/elevation sin/cos), panoramic action space as in Speaker-Follower.
LEO+: LEO plus speaker-generated synthetic instructions (M'=3 augmented plus M=3 original) and mixed IL+RL loss; also plugged into SMNA and EnvDrop.

setting.backbone: LSTM encoder-decoder seq2seq (Speaker-Follower Follower base) with ResNet visual features, trained from scratch
setting.training_data: R2R train (3 instructions per trajectory); LEO+ adds Speaker-Follower augmented trajectories with 3 speaker-generated instructions each, plus IL+RL
setting.privileged: none for the model, but multi-instruction setting feeds all 3 test instructions of a trajectory

results: LEO+ reaches 65 SR / 62 SPL on R2R test-unseen with three instructions, about 9 points SPL above the previous best non-test-exploring result (Prevalent 3-instr, 56). On a greedy Follower, LEO raises unseen SPL from 25 to 31 (1 instruction) and 26 to 41 (3 instructions), and adds +9 and +12 SPL on SMNA and EnvDrop.
limitations: Test-time multi-instruction gains rely on having several instructions per trajectory, which is unrealistic; single-instruction gains are much smaller.
Only mean/max/concat pooling and a shared encoder were explored; no learned cross-instruction reasoning.
Only R2R with older LSTM seq2seq agents evaluated; the fair-comparison table mixes settings with different numbers of test instructions.
